key_insight: The paper couples a sharp-crack deep energy method with thermoelastic fracture so temperature, displacement, and crack growth are solved together without phase-field regularization.
engineering_relevance: It enables physics-informed prediction of thermo-mechanical crack initiation and path evolution in cracked components under thermal loading.
method: Two neural networks represent temperature and displacement, with the crack encoded by a discontinuous scalar embedding.
Displacement is enriched near the crack tip using a trainable Williams expansion.
Training alternates between thermal conduction and thermoelastic energy minimization with Monte Carlo integration and adaptive point sampling.
evidence_signal: The method matches published benchmark results closely, including a stress intensity factor error of 0.11% and crack initiation within one load step on a graded shear test.
watch_item: The approach relies on careful contour-radius checks, tip enrichment, and stratified resampling, so implementation and training stability may be sensitive near crack tips and evolving geometries.
paper_title: An extended deep energy method for thermo-mechanical crack propagation
